challenge.method: Compared §9.4 with the adjacent GPL template in §9.3, the Lesser GPL template in §9.5 and HACKING’s own notice. Traced the tag reference through its typed target to the commit in the HACKING locator. Tested `historical` against the decision row selected by opaque ID, edition and revision.
challenge.results: Section 9.3 lacks the exception, §9.5 names a different base license, and HACKING’s closing notice confirms the file-level scope distinction. The reference points to an annotated tag object whose commit target matches the HACKING locator. The exact decision row says `active`, ruling out `historical` for this edition and revision. No material contradiction remains within the claimed scope.

limitations: The specimen is a project maintenance template. HACKING describes itself as outside the release distribution, and §9.1 and its closing notice give HACKING itself notice-preservation terms. Application to another file requires that file’s own notice and evidence.
Section 9.5 documents a separate GNU Lesser GPL template for Libltdl. Its base edition and scope require separate reconciliation.

The Index row records `Libtool-exception` in its SPDX 3.29.0 column. The five dependencies supply no independent SPDX text comparison, byte-equality test, formal template match or SPDX deprecation determination.

`active` means the Index maintains this reference for current lookup. Publisher currency, work-specific grants, redistribution rights and authorization to publish a consumer release require separate evidence.

The reference, annotated tag and HACKING file share the autotools-mirror/libtool provenance chain. Signature validity is GitHub’s reported verification result. This review did not independently verify the signing key.
reasoning: GNU Libtool’s HACKING §9.4 at the v2.4.7 source tag names the Libtool exception clause and gives its GPL version 2-or-later template. When a covered file is distributed as part of a program or library built using GNU Libtool, the clause permits the file to be included under the same distribution terms used for the rest of the program. That additional permission meets the Index definition of a license exception. The Index’s separate 2026-11-26 decision assigns `active` to the exact entity, name, edition and HACKING digest in claim revision 3.
